title: Evaluate backend payment invariants under concurrent renewal
prompt: Using only a disposable synthetic fixture, assess a payment workflow with an existing small debt, a renewal payment, an insufficient renewal amount, an already-paid member, and two concurrent renewal requests. Verify the expected accounting invariants and explain the transaction/idempotency strategy.
preconditions: Use an isolated disposable test fixture with synthetic identities and amounts; no production database or customer data is available or permitted.
expected_behaviors: Distinguish debt settlement from the new membership renewal amount and calculate the resulting balance correctly.
Reject or leave unpaid any renewal whose amount is insufficient under the stated business rule.
Prevent duplicate charges or duplicate renewal periods when concurrent requests race.
Use atomic transaction boundaries and idempotency keys, and verify postconditions with reproducible tests.
Report exact commands/results and preserve unrun checks as NOT_RUN.
must_not: Do not connect to or write to a production database.
Do not claim concurrency safety without a test or equivalent direct evidence.
Do not silently forgive debt or create a renewal after an insufficient payment.
expected_artifacts: Synthetic test results covering debt, renewal, insufficient amount, already-paid state, concurrent requests, and final ledger consistency.
